extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, CRU/TC supervisory staff, and patent practitioners involved in ex parte reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive criteria for deciding, assigning, and processing ex parte reexamination requests under 35 U.S.C. 302–305, including time limits, examiner assignment, required showings (substantial new question of patentability), and handling of copending/repeated requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Assignment Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRU SPRS will assign the reexamination request to an examiner different from the examiner(s) who examined the patent application (normal circumstances). An examiner who was involved in any part of the examination of the patent (e.g., preparing/signing an action) or who was a conferee in an appeal conference or panel review is generally excluded from assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: where the original examiner is the only examiner with adequate knowledge of the relevant technology, assignment to the original examiner may occur but must be approved by the CRU Director and that approval must be stated in the decision or indicated by the CRU Director's signature. If an earlier reexamination is still ongoing, the same examiner may be assigned the new reexamination. The conferee is considered to have participated in preparing the Office action that preceded the conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copending Reissue and Reexamination Assignment Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reissue application is pending for a patent and a reexamination request is filed (or vice versa), assignment and handling of the proceedings follow specified rules to avoid conflicts and to determine which examiner will handle merged or parallel proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If merged by OPLA, the merged proceeding is generally handled by the examiner handling the reissue application; however, if that examiner was involved in the original examination of the patent (e.g., prepared/signed an action) or was involved in the parent application, a different examiner will be assigned and the reissue may be transferred. If reexamination already ordered, OPLA should be notified promptly to consider merger; paper files should be scanned into the Image File Wrapper (IFW) before notifying OPLA. If reexamination has not been ordered, the SPRS will ensure parallel reissue application is not assigned or acted upon until decision on the reexamination request is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of Inadvertent Assignment to an Original Examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination is inadvertently assigned to an 'original examiner', the patent owner or third-party requester who objects must promptly file a paper notifying the Office within two months of the first Office action or communication indicating the examiner assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reassignment will be addressed case-by-case. Failure to timely notify (within two months) generally precludes reassignment consideration. Assignment to the original examiner, by itself, is not grounds for vacating Office decisions or restarting the reexamination. If a notifying paper lacks a right of entry, the Office may waive rules to enter and consider it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer Procedure for Reexamination Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A reexamination request is normally assigned to a CRU art unit that examines the technology in which the patent is classified; SPRSs may request transfer of a reexamination to another art unit if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CRU SPRS desiring transfer must obtain consent of the SPRS of the receiving art unit; any unresolved conflicts are decided by the CRU Director. Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 305, transfers must be conducted with special dispatch; if accepted, the new CRU SPRS assigns the request to an examiner in that unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Reporting for Reexamination Activities
rubrics_metrics.description: All USPTO personnel must report all time expended on reexamination activities accurately on their Time and Attendance Reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include supervisory activities, copying, typing, and docketing when reporting time spent on reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination at the Director's Initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may determine at any time during a patent's enforceability that a substantial new question of patentability is raised and may initiate ex parte reexamination without a request or fee (37 CFR 1.520).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such Director-initiated reexaminations are rare and reserved for compelling circumstances after review of all facts; authority has been delegated to the Deputy Commissioner for Patents who oversees the Office of Petitions. If an order is issued, OPLA prepares the decision in cooperation with CRU/TC and the decision becomes part of the patent file and is mailed to the patent owner. The Director will not normally consider public requests to order reexamination on the Director's initiative; members of the public should file a regular request under 37 CFR 1.510.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for Decision on Request Filed under 35 U.S.C. 302
rubrics_metrics.description: Within three months following the filing of a request for reexamination under section 302, the Director (or examiner under delegation) will determine whether a substantial new question of patentability affecting any claim is raised (35 U.S.C. 303(a); 37 CFR 1.515(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 3-month period ends on a weekend or federal holiday in D.C., the determination must be mailed by the preceding business day. Determination may be made at any time during the patent's enforceability period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination Basis — Claims in Effect and Exclusions from Consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's determination whether to order reexamination is based on the claims in effect at the time of the determination; certain submitted statements or amendments will not be considered when making the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement and accompanying information submitted pursuant to § 1.501(a)(2) will not be considered when deciding the request. Amendments (1) presented with the request by the patent owner, (2) filed in a pending reexamination where certificate not issued, or (3) submitted in a reissue application on which no reissue patent has issued, will not be considered when deciding requests. The order for reexamination should discuss whether a substantial new question is raised but SHOULD NOT reject claims; any rejection is made in the first Office action on patentability after the patent owner statement/reply period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litigation Search Before Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making a determination on a request filed under 35 U.S.C. 302, a litigation search from TSS of the CRU or STIC must be done to check if the patent has been or is involved in litigation; the 'Litigation Review' box on the reexamination jacket form should be completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the litigation search and the reexamination file history should be placed in the reexamination IFW. If litigation has occurred or is occurring, the request must be brought promptly to the attention of the CRU SPRS for review to ensure conformity with Office litigation policy (see MPEP § 2286). If a litigation records search is already on file, the examiner need not repeat or update it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Set Forth Pertinency and Manner of Applying Cited Art
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 302 requires that the request 'set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester fails to apply the art to certain claims, the requester is not statutorily entitled to reexamination of those claims. Failure to set forth pertinency and manner of applying cited art to any requested claim may result in no filing date being awarded to the request. If requester chooses not to request reexamination for a claim, that claim will generally not be reexamined by the Office unless the Office exercises discretion to reexamine it or initiates reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 303(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'Substantial New Question of Patentability'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'substantial new question of patentability' exists where the prior art patents and printed publications raise a substantial likelihood that a reasonable examiner would consider the prior art important in deciding whether the claim is patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a question is not present if the same question has already been (A) decided in a final holding of invalidity by a federal court on the merits after appeals, (B) decided in an earlier concluded Office examination or review of the patent, or (C) raised to or by the Office in a pending reexamination or supplemental examination. If the new art is merely cumulative to art already fully considered by the Office, it may not raise a substantial new question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner Should Indicate Initial Position on Identified Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should indicate, insofar as possible, his or her initial position on all issues identified in the request filed under 35 U.S.C. 302 or raised by the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This initial position allows the patent owner statement and requester reply to address those issues; examiners should limit discussion in the order to whether a substantial new question has been raised and avoid making patentability determinations in the order itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Construction Standard for Reexamination Determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: In making the determination of whether to order reexamination (and during examination), the Office will determine the proper meaning of patent claims by giving the claims their broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification (In re Yamamoto), except for expired patents where Phillips construction applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For expired patents in reexamination, claim construction follows Phillips v. AWH Corp. (ordinary and customary meaning as understood by a person of ordinary skill in the art at the time of the invention). Statements submitted under 35 U.S.C. 301(a)(2) are limited to determining proper meaning only in proceedings ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304; they are not considered for ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope Limitation to Requested Claims and Office Discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: It is only necessary to establish a substantial new question of patentability as to one claim to grant reexamination, and the Office's review will generally be limited to the claims for which reexamination was requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester wanted all claims reexamined, they had the opportunity to include them in the request. The Office may, however, choose to reexamine claims not requested at its discretion or may initiate reexamination on non-requested claims under 35 U.S.C. 303(a). Case law (e.g., Sony Computer Entertainment America Inc. v. Dudas) confirms that reexamination can be limited to requested claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Second or Subsequent Requests During Pending Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When a second or subsequent request for ex parte reexamination is filed while a first is pending, whether reexamination is ordered depends on whether the prior art cited raises a 'different' substantial new question of patentability for the claims in effect at the time of determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the second request cites art that raises the same substantial new question as the pending reexamination, the second request should be denied. If it raises a different substantial new question for some claims but not others, grant in part. The later requester must independently provide a different substantial new question with respect to the claims in effect at the time. The second/subsequent request may include information directed to proposed new/amended claims in the pending reexamination, to permit examination of the entire patent package when appropriate. If a second/subsequent request appears filed for harassment and a petitioner shows this (e.g., by petition under 37 CFR 1.182), prosecution on the second/subsequent reexamination may be suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality and Review of Denials
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination by the Director (or examiner under delegation) that no substantial new question of patentability has been raised is final and nonappealable, subject to a petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 37 CFR 1.515(c), the requester may seek review by petition to the Director under § 1.181 within one month of the mailing date of the examiner's determination refusing ex parte reexamination. If no timely petition is filed, or petition affirms the denial, the determination is final and nonappealable. If no substantial new question is found, a portion of the reexamination fee may be refunded per § 1.26(c).
